answer: Polkadot-style registrar judgements make each agent identity face real scrutiny. First, the operator posts an on-chain identity and locks a 20 POA deposit. Second, a bonded registrar, paid a $25 fee, checks a domain, an inbox and a live video call. Third, it signs a KnownGood judgement; only judged keys may attest, and a fake loses it and burns the deposit. A farm wanting 500 seats needs 500 domains, 500 calls, $12,500 in fees and 10,000 POA locked. Think of a customs house on the wharf: crates land freely, but only stamped cargo climbs the terrace road up the mesa to market.
